import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import seaborn as sns

# Load the dataset
df = pd.read_csv('data/customer_segments.csv')

# Handle missing values in Income for accurate calculations and plotting
df.dropna(subset=['Income'], inplace=True)

# Calculate total spending across all product categories
mnt_cols = ['MntWines', 'MntFruits', 'MntMeatProducts', 'MntFishProducts', 'MntSweetProducts', 'MntGoldProds']
df['Total_Mnt'] = df[mnt_cols].sum(axis=1)

# Filter out extreme income outliers for a clearer visualization of the main data distribution.
# The maximum income value (666666.0) is an extreme outlier that compresses the x-axis.
# We'll cap the income displayed at the 99th percentile to focus on the majority of customers.
income_upper_bound = df['Income'].quantile(0.99)
df_filtered = df[df['Income'] <= income_upper_bound].copy() # Use .copy() to avoid SettingWithCopyWarning

# Create the scatter plot
plt.figure(figsize=(12, 8))
sns.scatterplot(data=df_filtered, x='Income', y='Total_Mnt', hue='Education',
                palette='viridis', alpha=0.7, s=60, linewidth=0)

# Add title and labels
plt.title('Customer Spending vs. Income by Education Level (Top 1% Income Excluded)', fontsize=16, weight='bold')
plt.xlabel('Income', fontsize=12)
plt.ylabel('Total Amount Spent on Products', fontsize=12)

# Improve legend and grid
plt.legend(title='Education Level', bbox_to_anchor=(1.02, 1), loc='upper left', borderaxespad=0)
plt.grid(True, linestyle='--', alpha=0.6)

# Enhance plot aesthetics
plt.xticks(fontsize=10)
plt.yticks(fontsize=10)
plt.ticklabel_format(style='plain', axis='x') # Prevent scientific notation for x-axis if not needed

# Adjust layout to prevent elements from overlapping, especially the legend
plt.tight_layout()

# Save the figure
plt.savefig('output.png', bbox_inches='tight', dpi=150)

import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

df = pd.read_csv('data/customer_segments.csv')

# Handle missing values in Income for accurate calculations and plotting
df.dropna(subset=['Income'], inplace=True)

# Calculate total spending across all product categories
mnt_cols = ['MntWines', 'MntFruits', 'MntMeatProducts', 'MntFishProducts', 'MntSweetProducts', 'MntGoldProds']

# Filter out extreme income outliers for a clearer visualization of the main data distribution.

# We'll cap the income displayed at the 99th percentile to focus on the majority of customers.
income_upper_bound = df['Income'].quantile(0.99)
df_filtered = df[df['Income'] <= income_upper_bound].copy() # Use .copy() to avoid SettingWithCopyWarning

# Create the scatter plot
plt.figure(figsize=(12, 8))
sns.scatterplot(data=df_filtered, x='Income', y='Total_Mnt', hue='Education',
                palette='viridis', alpha=0.7, s=60, linewidth=0)

# Add title and labels
plt.title('Customer Spending vs. Income by Education Level (Top 1% Income Excluded)', fontsize=16, weight='bold')
plt.xlabel('Income', fontsize=12)
plt.ylabel('Total Amount Spent on Products', fontsize=12)

# Improve legend and grid
plt.legend(title='Education Level', bbox_to_anchor=(1.02, 1), loc='upper left', borderaxespad=0)

# Enhance plot aesthetics
